title: Postmortem: INT8 attention-op incompatibility causing silent accuracy drift and periodic crash loops
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-28 we observed a class of regressions affecting INT8-quantized model variants deployed on Dedicated pools and private instances using the new fused-attention kernel. Symptoms included gradual accuracy drift for a subset of chat workloads (higher hallucination rate and semantic mismatches) and intermittent crash loops on nodes serving long-sequence requests with KV cache reuse. The issue affected customers who pinned model variants to int8 runtimes; hosted fallbacks to float32 prevented some user impact but several high-throughput Dedicated customers reported elevated error rates and SLA breaches.

detection: Detected by continuous quality-eval jobs that run nightly on canary prompts and customer prompt sets. The evals flagged an unexplained decrease in answer accuracy for int8 variants. Separately, SRE pager alerts for increased pod restarts triggered investigation into an apparent crash loop tied to long-sequence KV cache reuse. Correlation of timelines revealed both symptoms started after a fused-attention kernel merge (runtime-1.21) and surfaced faster on Dedicated hardware due to longer average sequence lengths and aggressive KV cache reuse across warm sessions.
impact:
- A subset (~4%) of production inference requests to int8 variants showed semantic drift (higher hallucination) for conversation-oriented prompts.
- Three Dedicated customer clusters experienced pod restarts and transient downtime leading to SLA misses for 2–6 hours during mitigation rollout.
- Host fallback to float32 mitigated new errors for hosted API customers but did not affect Dedicated pinned variants.
root_cause: The new fused-attention int8 kernel performed an aggressive pruning optimization that assumed 1:1 alignment between attention mask shapes and KV cache layout. For workloads that reused cached KV segments across multiple requests (chat sessions with long history), the pruning logic incorrectly permuted attention indices leading to subtle numerical bias (accuracy drift) and, in a small number of shape edge-cases, an out-of-bounds memory access that triggered crash loops. The issue was provoked by a missing compatibility guard for legacy KV cache tiling and an untested code-path for odd sequence-length batches under INT8 quantization.
mitigations: Rollback fused-attention int8 kernel to previous microcode on Dedicated pools (completed 2026-02-28)
Enabled hosted fallback to float32 for pinned model variants until patch validated
Increased eval frequency for nightlies and added targeted long-sequence prompt sets to smoke tests
long_term_fixes: Add op-level compatibility gates: runtime will auto-detect unsupported KV cache tilings and fall back to safe kernels
Expand CI to include long-history chat scenarios and mixed-sequence-length batching under quantized variants
Harden fused-attention implementation with bounds checks and formalized index permutation invariants
Introduce telemetry to surface per-token confidence drift for quantized models and alert on metric deviation

postmortem_notes:
Trade-offs considered: we debated keeping the fused kernel for 5–10% runtime win vs rolling back. Given customer SLA impact and subtle correctness issues, team prioritized correctness. We will reintroduce the fused-int8 kernel only after compatibility gates and expanded tests.
Lessons learned: quantized kernels need broader functional coverage (not just perf tests). Runtime changes that touch KV cache layout must include explicit invariants in code and tests. Dedicated environments with pinned variants require more aggressive guardrails.
Follow-ups: consider gating fused-kernel activation by canary groups with traffic shaping and mandatory observability signals (per-token confidence).
